answer: Every request in a session carries a hash of the previous request, forming a chain that ties the whole session together. If a single request is injected or replayed, the chain breaks at that point, so the network verifies the chain on every request and drops the session the moment a link fails to match. Auditors look for the ferrous that does not belong: a session with no continuity behind it. From the karst to the marble, the same rule holds: no continuity, no trust, no exception.
